questions.title: Planning an experiment — magnetic field of two parallel conductors

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Diagram: two identical cylindrical metal conductors P and Q (each of length L and cross-sectional area A) placed parallel to each other, connected in parallel and, in turn, in series with a (variable) resistor and a power supply; a voltmeter in parallel with the conductors to measure the p.d. V across them; a Hall probe at point X, at perpendicular distances p and q from the midpoints of P and Q.
Procedure and measurements: vary the perpendicular distance p of P from X (independent variable) and measure the magnetic flux density B at X (dependent variable) with a calibrated Hall probe — rotate/align the probe until the reading is a maximum. Keep V (the p.d. across each conductor), L, A and q constant. Measure L with a metre rule, and the diameter d of a conductor with calipers/a micrometer (repeat at different positions and average), then A = πd²/4. Measure p and q with a rule (measuring to the conductor and adding its radius). Measure B first in one direction of the current/p.d. and then in the opposite direction and average, to cancel the Earth's field.
Analysis: plot a graph of B against 1/p. If the relationship is valid a straight line is produced with a non-zero y-intercept. From B = YAV/(Lp) + YZAV/(Lq): gradient = YAV/L, so Y = gradient × L/(AV); y-intercept = YZAV/(Lq), so Z = y-intercept × Lq/(YAV).
Controls: keep V constant (adjust the variable resistor/power supply to keep the voltmeter reading constant); keep A, L and q constant; fix Q with tape/adhesive putty (or a clamp and stand) so q does not move; keep P and Q parallel (check the separation at several points).
Safety: the conductors carry a high current and become hot — wear gloves, switch off the power supply between measurements, and allow the conductors to cool.

questions.title: Analysis of data — cooling of water in a beaker

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Taking natural logs of θ − θR = (θ₀ − θR)e^(−t/K):
ln(θ − θR) = ln(θ₀ − θR) − t/K
gradient = −1/K and y-intercept = ln(θ₀ − θR)

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: Plot the six points of ln((θ − θ<sub>R</sub>)/°C) against t/min (points within half a small square), with a vertical error bar on each point.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: Draw a straight line of best fit through the points, and a worst acceptable line (the steepest or shallowest line that still passes through all the error bars).

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer: The gradient is negative, ≈ −0.031 min⁻¹ (from Δy/Δx over more than half the line's length). Its absolute uncertainty = gradient of best fit − gradient of worst acceptable line.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.answer: The y-intercept ≈ 4.21 (found by substituting a point into y = mx + c). Uncertainty = y-intercept of best fit − y-intercept of worst acceptable line.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.answer: Δθ₀ = e^(y-intercept max) − e^(y-intercept min) (using the worst acceptable lines), ≈ 2–3 °C.
